correctness.rationale: The propagator factorizes because the hypercube adjacency is a sum of commuting bit flips. Diagonal corrections preserve entry magnitudes, forcing \(|\cos(t/n)|=|\sin(t/n)|\) and hence the discrete uniform-mixing times. At every such time the Hadamard-to-propagator ratio is the rank-one phase matrix \(\rho^{-h(x)}\rho^{-h(y)}\), whose diagonal factorization is unique up to scalars. Any loop-singleton sequence of total time \(T\) assigns each vertex an accumulated nonnegative time in \([0,T]\); therefore the required fourth-root phase set must fit in a directed arc of length \(T\). The exact arc lengths are \(\pi/2\), \(\pi\), and \(3\pi/2\), and explicit masks attain them. This proves both lower and upper bounds for every \(n\ge1\).

value.rationale: The source explicitly treats reducing evolution time as a central simplification objective and gives a fast parallel-Hadamard construction. The exact lower bound turns those timings into an optimality theorem: it certifies that the \(5\pi/2\) two-qubit implementation and the \(3\pi/2\) per-side phase cost for \(n\ge3\) cannot be improved merely by rearranging or splitting loop masks, and it identifies the distinct \(5\pi/4\) one-qubit optimum. This pinpoints which architectural ingredient must change for any further speedup, so the result is a structural design constraint rather than a routine recomputation.
